rationale: Exact camera geometry exposes 8.88% median maximum affine corner error even when the notch and lower edges are known. Complete-shape hard gates add no real crops. Test projective geometry using visible outline support first.
cases: All 16 original/occluded synthetic pairs, plus a separate exact-complete-body diagnostic on the 16 originals. No selection by previous crop success.
mainMethod: Use the existing projective outline model and its lower-edge estimator. Remove paper-color/purity/diameter-contrast terms and the corresponding color gates for this offline body-only arm. Retain outline/edge support, bounds and perspective constraints. No annotated corners enter proposals.
fields: For the measured arm, use the frozen automatically prompted MobileSAM body and source RGB. Material input is neutral and cannot favor a crop. The coarse CNN is not a hard support gate.
oracleControl: Use the known physical synthetic body only to diagnose the projective model and optimizer ceiling. Label clearly as an oracle; never combine these crops with predicted-field success counts. Exact corners enter scoring only.
fixedPolicy: Same model defaults, current maxSize=650, current orientation exploration and support thresholds. No per-case parameter adjustment. Freeze source before running.
measurement: Report proposal counts, maximum per-corner error normalized by mean source-square side, counts below 1%, 3% and 5%, before/after occlusion changes and runtime. Inspect all proposals and rejections.
decision: Only after this identifies a reliable projective construction, evaluate on the fixed real-photo cohorts with unchanged material masks and downstream geometry/paper/editor checks. If visible outlines still bias covered corners, test soft visibility weighting separately; do not blindly union masks.
qaDependency: Wait for the live shape-visibility-v1 full test suite to terminate before the next substantial fitting run.
limitations: Sixteen training-source geometries from one procedural family; not held-out generalization.
The ellipse-cap outline model may remain unsuitable for decorative caps; no claim otherwise.
This isolates crop geometry, not hidden material recovery or complete-template accuracy.
